subject: Post-call recap: vector index fit + evaluation plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire@lexisearch.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: vector index fit + evaluation plan

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while you validate model fit on your side.

Call highlights (very short):
- Use case: product search + recommendations for knowledge-base + small catalog (~250k docs).
- Main success metrics you care about: recall@10 (human judged), MRR, and reduction in stale redirects (customer complaints).
- Current stack: in-house MiniLM embeddings (384d). You observed some topic drift and poor separation on short queries.

Preliminary Redwood recommendations (opinionated):
1) Evaluate two candidate embedding families: 
   - rw-embed-v1 (1536-d, Redwood-curated, optimized for semantic similarity)
   - sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L12-v2 (384-d, fast baseline)
2) Use a 1k-query benchmark set (mix of short navigational queries and long multi-sentence intents). We'll run recall@10, MRR, and embedding cosine distance distributions.
3) Dimensionality check: compare 384d vs 1536d. Higher-d may improve separation but costs storage/search latency. We'll include a PCA explained-variance curve in the report.
4) Drift signal: baseline drift test by month-over-month centroid shift and fraction of outlier queries (>3 std dev).

Attached: a starter prompt set (prompt_set_v2.txt), sample queries (sample_queries.csv) and a template QC workbook (benchmark_results_qc.xlsx). I ran a quick local pass with rw-embed-v1 on a 50k sample — see 'Quick notes' tab in the workbook.

Next steps (action owners):
- Claire: confirm access to a 1k production-ish query sample or let us pull anonymized logs (we can provide sanitization steps). Target: by Apr 14.
- Monica: run the initial rw-embed-v1 vs MiniLM batch, produce recall@10 and MRR numbers (deadline Apr 16).
- Rafael: prepare a short A/B plan for index rollout and cost delta estimates.

If that looks right I'll tee up a quick sandbox run and share a Drive link for the detailed results.

Thanks — Rafael
--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.txt (text file of labeled queries), sample_queries.csv (100 example queries), benchmark_results_qc.xlsx (template)

From: Claire Thompson <claire@lexisearch.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, LexiSearch Data Science Team <ds-team@lexisearch.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: vector index fit + evaluation plan

Thanks Rafa — this is exactly the kind of plan I wanted. Quick answers:
- I can provide 1.2k anonymized queries (we'll strip user ids). I'll upload to your Drive unless you prefer us to send via S3.
- Our main constraint is latency: today our search tail (p95) is ~120ms; we'd prefer not to double that.
- We expect to continue using our existing retrieval pipeline (Elasticsearch + FAISS) so recommendations on quantization/approximate search parameters would be helpful.

One note: our dataset has a long tail of single-sentence product codes where MiniLM is doing okay; the problems happen with multi-paragraph support articles. If rw-embed-v1 improves MRR there is a clear business case.

I'll upload the queries by EOD Thu (Apr 9). S3 link pref: s3://lexisearch-share/anon/vec-eval-2026-04-07.csv.

Claire

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: vector index fit + evaluation plan

Monica — forwarding Claire's confirmation. She prefers S3; Claire said she'll upload the 1.2k anon queries by EOD Thu (Apr 9). Please treat this as high priority for the technical bench.

Technical checklist for the run (short and tactical):
- Data: use the S3 sample; ensure we strip any remaining PII (we have a sanitization script in /playbooks/data-san).
- Models to ingest: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L12-v2 (384d; baseline) and rw-embed-v1 (1536d; Redwood).
- Index config: test with FAISS HNSW (efConstruction 200, M=32) and PQ-quantized IVF for the 1536-d run to estimate storage tradeoffs.
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, recall gap on short vs long queries, cosine similarity distributions, PCA explained variance (top 10 components).
- Drift check: compute centroid shift vs their last-month sample (if available) and fraction of queries with cosine max < 0.2 (possible OOD).
- Perf: measure embedding compute time (ms/query), index search p50/p95 latency.

Deliverables (target Apr 16):
- Short one-page summary with recommended model and config for production (include cost delta).
- Detailed workbook (benchmark_results_qc.xlsx) with raw numbers and plots.
- A short A/B rollout plan (canary buckets, fallback).

I'll draft the one-pager once you post initial numbers. Ping me if you need assistance with PQ params or if GPU/CPU resource limits surface.

Rafael

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Claire Thompson <claire@lexisearch.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: vector index fit + evaluation plan

Thanks — I pulled the S3 file (s3://lexisearch-share/anon/vec-eval-2026-04-07.csv) and kicked off the batch runs this morning. Quick status:

What I ran so far (progress):
- Sample sanity checks and PII scrub completed (script: scripts/sanitize_queries.py).
- Baseline MiniLM (384d) run finished on 50k sample; results in first tab of the workbook. Preliminary recall@10 ~ 0.72, MRR 0.58 on short queries, much lower (recall@10 0.44) on long support-article intents.
- rw-embed-v1 1536d run started; early signs: larger cosine separation on long-form queries, but embedding compute is ~2.1x slower and index size ~3x.

Early observations (don't treat as final):
- PCA on rw-embed-v1: first 10 components explain ~62% variance (suggests good spread).
- Cosine max distribution shifts from a tight cluster (MiniLM) to a wider spread for rw-embed-v1, which corresponds to better MRR on long queries in the pilot.
- Drift signal: ~4.2% of queries are below 0.15 cosine max vs their monthly centroid — flagging those as potential OOD.

Next actions (Monica -> Rafael -> Claire):
- I'll finish full-run metrics and populate benchmark_results_qc.xlsx by Apr 16 (target).
- Rafael: please draft the one-pager A/B plan and include a cost estimate for the 1536-d deployment (storage + CPU/GPU embed cost).
- Claire: once you review the workbook we can pick the rollout cadence; my suggestion is a 5% canary for 3 days then 25% for a week if MRR lift > 6% on long queries.

I'll attach the run logs and a small notebook with PCA plots to the Drive link when the full run finishes.

—Monica
